about.title: Hello, I'm
about.name: Esther.
paragraphs: As a digital project manager and delivery partner, I'm the person you call when you have a digital ambition that needs to become real.

Moving quickly to understand your unique challenges comes naturally to me. Leading a strategic whiteboard session with your management team or running a technical review with your developers, both feel equally at home. My core strength is acting as the connective tissue across disciplines - bridging the gap between IT, creative, and business, and making sure complex work actually crosses the finish line.

Straightforward answers and tangible action win over lengthy reports, every time. When I work with you, you will always know where things stand - and you will always get a partner who takes ownership of the work.

items.label: 01 / BRAND + WEBSITE
items.title: A travel companion, not another tour guide.
items.needed: Dennis writes, answers and shows up himself. The brand needed to make that personal trust visible, while giving culturally curious travelers the context and calm they look for before choosing a day together.
made: Tone of voice and reply templates
items.direction: Cream creates the feeling of paper, deep purple carries the story and orange appears only where it matters. A hand-drawn portrait behaves like Dennis's signature. Bebas Neue, Outfit and Caveat keep the system direct, readable and personal.
items.outcome: Dennis now has one coherent system for the website, email, replies, business cards, LinkedIn, Instagram and listings. Every touchpoint follows the same test: different, calm, trusted and human.
items.credits: Brand strategy, identity, website and brandbook by Es Venture.

studio.title: Small on purpose. Serious about the work.
paragraphs: I'm Esther. I spent years working on digital projects inside companies. Booking systems, platforms, migrations. My job was making sure the thing actually got finished, with all the parties that come with it. I still do that work as a Digital Delivery Manager.

What struck me there: the longer a project ran, the further it drifted from what it was actually about. Months of documents, and only at the very end something to look at. While what I love most is exactly that. Putting what lives in someone's head onto a screen, so you can react to it together.

That's why Es Venture exists. Here I work small and fast, with entrepreneurs who are the face of their own business. No steering committee, no months-long tracks. You sit with the person who actually makes it.

Here's how it goes: we start with a conversation in which I probably ask too much. How do your customers talk about you, what are you secretly proud of, which competitor's website annoys you and why exactly. Almost always, that's where the idea comes out that the rest will lean on.

Then you see something fast. A design, or a prototype you can really click through. Often you won't like it at first, and that's fine. That's how we find out what it should become. After that I can spend hours on a single detail. A button that doesn't feel quite right, a colour that's slightly off. That's the best part.
My best ideas rarely come at my desk, by the way. Usually while running along the Westerpark.
If a project needs a photographer, developer or copywriter, I bring in someone I have known for years. You keep one point of contact.

servicesRoutes.title: Three ways to start with me.

items.title: I need a brand.
items.situation: You have a good business or a good idea, but you do not yet know how to explain it or what it should look like.
items.result: We work out what you offer, what people should remember, and how it should feel. I turn that into an identity you can keep using for years.
deliverables: the applications you need right away
items.example: Dennis Gerrits did not want to be a tour operator, but the Amsterdammer who shows you the city. That became an illustrated portrait mark, editorial typography and a palette of deep green, bordeaux and orange.

items.title: I need a website.
items.situation: You do not have a site yet, or the one you have does not show how good the work is.
items.result: We decide what a visitor needs to understand. I make the structure, the design and the site itself. Ready to use, at any size.
items.example: Studio Ingrid de Reuver had to feel warm and personal without the soft, beige photography template. That became an editorial serif, candid portraits and bright pink buttons, with a clear route from her story to her services and bookings.

items.title: I want to test an idea.
items.situation: You have an idea for an app or a service, and you do not want to pay for development before you know whether it works.
items.result: We pick the most important route someone takes through your product, work out how it should behave, and make a clickable prototype people can actually try.
deliverables: a recommendation for the next version
items.example: HAP was a recipe app idea. Instead of discussing the whole product, we made the first version clickable so you could see where people got stuck.

usp.title: What it came down to
usp.copy: The right visual direction usually starts before the colours and type. I look for the details, tone and point of view that make the business recognizable. That becomes the thread through the identity, the website and every interaction.
steps: Listen for the useful detail, not the loudest claim.
Turn the conversation into clear choices.
Make the thing tangible enough to show, test or launch.
paragraphs: The right direction does not start with colour or typography. First I look for the detail that makes a business recognisable.
For Dennis that was "a friend who knows the city, not a guide". For Ingrid it was that people feel at ease with her within two minutes.
That one thing becomes the thread through the brand, the site and every button.
